images.caption:
BPLDC no.: 08_04_000204
Page Title: Memnonium of SeTi
Collection: William Vaughn Tupper Scrapbook Collection
Album: On the Nile. Cairo to Luxor.
Call no.:  4098B.104 v31 (p.20)
Creator: Tupper, William Vaughn
Photographer: Beato, Antonio, ca. 1825-ca. 1903
Genre: Scrapbooks; Albumen prints
Extent: 1 photographic print mounted on page : albumen ; page 33 x 39 cm.
Description: Scrapbook page consists of one photograph of the Memnonium of Seti I Façade. The annotations included on this page recount the use of the Memnonium of Seti. 
Transcription: Of all Egypt it was the custom to send mummies here to rest a period of time and receive the blessings of Osiris. It was then carried to its ancestral burial ground- the mummy wrapt in embroidered linen was brought here on board a boat. We know nothing of what happened after the arrival of the mummy in peace at Abydos. "Probably the body assisted in the offereings  to the God for when the deceased had returned in peace from Abydos he boasted that he had breathed the breath of myrh, and inscense"- Ebers thinks that the earliest Asiatic imigrants settled here. Near here was the capital of Menes Ist historical king of Egypt. B.C. 5867. 23.20.
Notes: Page description supplied by cataloger, derived from captions and/or annotated information.; Page contains hand drawn hieroglyphics.
BPL Department: Print Department

Rights: No known restrictions.
